c.tagline: The 'Venice of the Alps,' where a canal-laced old town meets one of Europe's cleanest lakes

card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small market stalls

taxi.fare: Metered, roughly €3.50 flag fall plus per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard and reliable

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

walk: The old town canal district is compact and very walkable; the lakeside promenade extends further and is best explored on foot or by bike

safety.safety: Very safe city with a relaxed, family-friendly atmosphere
safety.crime: Petty theft near the old town and lakefront in peak summer is the main concern

hood_landmark.Vieille Ville (Old Town): The Palais de l'Isle on the Thiou river
hood_landmark.Lakefront (Bord du Lac): The Pont des Amours and lakeside gardens
hood_landmark.Talloires: The Abbaye de Talloires and the village port on Lake Annecy

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in the crowded old-town lanes and lakefront during peak summer.

hood_desc: The canal-laced medieval core with the Palais de l'Isle and pastel-colored buildings; the natural base for any visit.
The lake's edge promenade with gardens, swimming spots, and the romantic Pont des Amours, a short walk from the old town.

A lakeside village on Lake Annecy's quieter eastern shore, about 13 km from the old town, gathered around a small sailing port and the 11th-century Abbaye de Talloires, now a hotel. It is the base for the Roc de Chere nature reserve and is served by the lake boats in season.

transit.note: The old town and lakefront are best explored on foot or bike; buses serve outlying neighborhoods

transport.train: TGV and regional trains connect to Lyon, Geneva, and Paris
transport.bus: Regional buses connect to alpine villages and ski resorts
transport.ferry: Seasonal lake boat services connect Annecy to Talloires and other lakeside villages
transport.car: Well connected via the A41 motorway; the old town is pedestrian-friendly

landmarks: Palais de l'Ile
A 12th-century triangular stone prison-palace parting the Thiou canal like a ship's prow, deservedly among France's most photographed buildings.
Lac d'Annecy
Europe's famously purest lake, a turquoise Alpine mirror ringed by mountains, lidos, and a 40-kilometre cycling loop past storybook villages.
Vieille Ville (Old Town)
The 'Venice of the Alps', where pastel arcaded houses, flower-boxed bridges, and canal-side cafes crowd cobbled lanes along the rushing Thiou.
Chateau d'Annecy
The hulking hilltop castle of the Counts of Geneva, now a museum of Alpine art, lake ecology, and animated film overlooking the old town's rooftops.
Pont des Amours (Lovers' Bridge)
An elegant iron footbridge over the Vasse canal where, legend promises, couples who kiss mid-span will stay together for life.
Jardins de l'Europe
A leafy lakeside park of giant sequoias and swan-filled shores, linking the old town to Annecy's most beloved waterfront strolls.
Basilique de la Visitation
A hilltop basilica holding the relics of Saints Francis de Sales and Jane de Chantal, its campanile views embracing lake, town, and Alps.
Cathedrale Saint-Pierre
Annecy's 16th-century cathedral, where a young Jean-Jacques Rousseau once sang in the choir, served as Francis de Sales's episcopal seat.
Gorges du Fier
A day-trip catwalk bolted 25 metres above a thunderous river slot canyon, twisting past sculpted rock walls near Montrottier castle.
Le Semnoz
Annecy's home mountain in the Bauges massif, its summit pastures offering 360-degree Mont Blanc panoramas, summer luge runs, and winter skiing.

train.note: Gare d'Annecy is at the north end of the old town, five minutes' walk from the canals. Around a dozen direct trains a day run to Geneva in about 1h30m, alongside direct TGVs to Paris Gare de Lyon in roughly 3h40m and frequent TER services to Lyon Part-Dieu (about 2 hours) and Chambery (about 50 minutes). French and Swiss fares are sold separately, so buy the Geneva leg on SNCF Connect or from SBB rather than assuming a through ticket. This is an internal Schengen border, but carry ID as checks are sometimes made on the Geneva line.

bus.note: The gare routiere is directly in front of the railway station and is served by FlixBus, BlaBlaCar Bus and Alsa. Coaches from Geneva's international bus station run several times a day and take about an hour, more frequently on weekdays than Sundays. International tickets are bought online in advance; regional Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes coaches can be paid for on board. Ski-season shuttles to the resorts and to Geneva airport also use this stop.

intl.to: Talloires, Menthon-Saint-Bernard, Duingt & Sevrier (France) - lake boats from Quai Jules Philippe in the centre
intl.op: Compagnie des Bateaux du Lac d'Annecy

ferry.note: Boats leave from Place aux Bois on the quay in central Annecy, a two-minute walk from the old town. The Compagnie des Bateaux runs a Navibus shuttle around the lakeside villages as well as one-hour and 90-minute sightseeing cruises and lunch and dinner sailings aboard the Libellule. Sailings are frequent from April to October and heavily reduced in winter, so check the timetable before travelling. There is no international boat link - Lake Annecy lies entirely within France.
